A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same capacity-gap study and MiniMA/MiniChat experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original GPT2/Pythia distillation experiments, MiniMA benchmarks and ablations, and MiniChat evaluations, including additional results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds benchmark results, a teacher-assistant comparison, checkpoint sensitivity analysis and human assessments.

M1.justification: The main pruning procedure, distillation objective and MiniChat finetuning remain unchanged. Appendix O adds peripheral model adaptations: MiniLoong uses distributed attention for long contexts, and MiniMix uses mixture-of-experts upcycling. Their detailed procedures are deferred to model cards.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds evaluated coverage of ARC science questions, Winogrande commonsense coreference and TruthfulQA truthfulness. Existing training mixtures, primary benchmarks and chat datasets remain. The checkpoint comparison uses retained data and does not itself add task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds Mamba-2.8B to the main comparison, Mamba-1.4B and Qwen-1.8B to the smaller-model comparison, and teacher-assistant distillation to the ablations (Tables 3, 10 and 4). Figure 3 additionally includes Mixtral-8x7B and Phi2-2.8B as plotted compute-performance comparators. MiniMoE's new analytical resource comparison does not establish an experimental run.

E3.justification: New protocols include 25-shot ARC accuracy, 5-shot Winogrande accuracy, zero-shot TruthfulQA MC2 and an anonymized human Elo arena. Added controls use a 5B teacher assistant and approximately 90% versus 100% training-token checkpoints. TinyLLaMA changes from a 1,000B-token to a 2,500B-token checkpoint, and Phi compute assumptions change. LAMBADA's caption changes last-token to last-word accuracy without establishing that evaluation was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds teacher-assistant testing, sensitivity of the capacity-gap finding to checkpoint/token budget, and human-versus-GPT4 ranking validation (Table 4; Appendices B and M). Figure 2 also adds explicit scaling-fit analysis. Existing pruning ablations, training-loss analysis and appendix coding/writing cases are retained.

E5.justification: v2 adds a numerical teacher/student-size fit and Elo estimation with Spearman rank-correlation analysis. These extend statistical estimation beyond v1's heuristic optimum discussion. No corresponding run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests are supplied; Appendix B's description of deviations as insignificant is not accompanied by a test.

E6.justification: Original MiniMA/MiniChat table scores are retained, alongside substantial new results. MiniMA scores 43.43/65.98/39.76 on ARC/Winogrande/TruthfulQA, leading both listed baselines on ARC and TruthfulQA but trailing on Winogrande. The assistant variant trails MiniMA on all six primary benchmarks; MiniChat leads human Elo at 1013.9. TinyLLaMA results are replaced under its larger training budget, and Phi1.5's estimated compute changes from 30.4 to 17.5 billion TFLOPs. The revised Phoenix win-rate statement is inconsistent: 42.5% is stated, while Figure 6 shows 24/80 wins, or 30%.

T1.justification: Law 1 changes from T = S/0.4 to T = 2.498S - 11.498, approximately S/0.4. Table 1 adds symbolic FLOP and memory estimates for prior approaches. The pruning/loss equations and corollary remain, and no proof of the empirical law or impossible triangle is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 adds the impossible triangle among teacher size, student performance and additional compute as a central contribution, and extends the law's claimed stability to data scales. It strengthens fixed-budget efficiency wording. Whereas v1's abstract attributes 7B competitiveness specifically to MiniChat under GPT4 evaluation, v2 attributes it to MiniMA without that qualification.

C2.justification: v2 explains why empirical evidence is used instead of deriving the law, attributes teacher-assistant underperformance to a suboptimal distillation path, and interprets checkpoint results as data-scale stability. Appendix M adds a qualification about moderate human/GPT4 agreement, although interpreting correlation 0.54 as 54% consistency is problematic. Existing contamination and training-limitations discussions largely remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a model-collection link and model-card pointers, but removes v1's explicit 25%-versus-37% component-pruning percentages. Most hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain unchanged. Release wording changes from code/checkpoints being released to being planned for release; actual availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: The main literature background remains. v2 explicitly compares resource overheads of already cited teacher-assistant and MiniMoE approaches and strengthens its connection to already cited scaling-law research. It adds references concerning Mamba, Qwen, the new benchmarks, distributed attention, sparse upcycling and compute elasticity.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, hypotheses, observations and conclusion receive focused rewriting and clarification, with updated author/contact text. The principal section sequence and most method/setup prose remain. Added scientific appendix sections do not amount to wholesale narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from two columns to one, adds the impossible-triangle graphic, redraws the capacity-gap illustration with bar comparisons and a fitted scaling plot, and expands the compute-performance plot. New analysis and result displays are added. The main case table is shortened, while appendix cases and existing plots are resized or relocated.

improvement.justification: The teacher-assistant comparison, explicit scaling fit and human audit provide useful scrutiny missing from v1, modestly strengthening the paper's evidential basis. The gains are limited by the narrow 90%-versus-100% token comparison, incomplete human-study details and overinterpretation of rank correlation. v2 also introduces the incorrect Phoenix win-rate statement. These shortcomings and the broader claims prevent a substantial overall improvement.
